'''Hermann Anton Haus''' (August 8, 1925 – May 21, 2003) was an [[Austrians|Austrian]]-[[United States|American]] [[physicist]], [[electrical engineering|electrical engineer]], and [[Institute Professor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="Journal of Optics">{{cite journal
| author      = Jeffrey H Shapiro
| year        = 2004
| title       = Hermann Anton Haus, 1925–2003 (IN MEMORIAM)
| journal     = Journal of Optics B: Quantum and Semiclassical Optics
| volume      = 6
| issue       = 8
| pages       = S623–S625
| publisher   = European Optical Society Part
| doi         = 10.1088/1464-4266/6/8/E02
| url         = http://www.iop.org/EJ/abstract/1464-4266/6/8/E02
| access-date = 2008-12-22| doi-access = free
| url-access  = subscription
}}</ref> Haus' research and teaching ranged from fundamental investigations of [[quantum uncertainty]] as manifested in [[optical communications]] to the practical generation of ultra-short optical pulses. In 1994, the [[Optical Society of America]] recognized Dr. Haus' contributions with its [http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/ivesquinn/ Frederic Ives Medal], the society's highest award. He also received OSA's [[Charles Hard Townes Award|Charles Hard Townes]] Medal in 1987, and was a Fellow of the society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hermann A. Haus {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Hermann_A_Haus |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref> Haus authored or co-authored eight books (see section below), published nearly 300 articles, and presented his work at virtually every major conference and symposium on laser and quantum electronics and quantum optics around the world. He was awarded the National Medal of Science in 1995 and was adopted into RPI's Alumni Hall of Fame in 2007.

He was a grandson of the Austrian admiral [[Anton Haus]]. His father, [[Otto Maximilian Haus]], was a leading Slovenian doctor who investigated [[tuberculosis]]. The tomb of his great-grandmother Marija Haus (Walter) is still in [[Bubnjarci]], Croatia.

== Books authored or co-authored by Prof. Haus ==
*[https://isbnsearch.org/isbn/9780262582322 H. A. Haus and R. B. Adler, Circuit Theory of Linear Noisy Networks (The MIT Press, 1959).]
*[https://isbnsearch.org/isbn/9780262190053 H. A. Haus, Noise in Electron Devices (The MIT Press, 1959)]
*[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/1876151 H. A. Haus and J. P. Penhune, Case Studies in Electromagnetism: Problems with Solutions (Wiley, 1960).]
*[https://isbnsearch.org/isbn/9780262160193 P. Penfield and H. A. Haus, Electrodynamics of Moving Media (The MIT Press, 1967).]
*[https://isbnsearch.org/isbn/0139460535 H. A. Haus, Waves and Fields in Optoelectronics (Prentice Hall, Incorporated, 1984).]
*[https://isbnsearch.org/isbn/013249020X H. A. Haus and J. R. Melcher, Electromagnetic Fields and Energy (Prentice Hall, 1989).]
*[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-04190-1 H. A. Haus, Electromagnetic Noise and Quantum Optical Measurements (Springer Science & Business Media, 2000).]
*[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4615-0855-7 C. Manolatou and H. A. Haus, Passive Components for Dense Optical Integration (Springer Science & Business Media, 2002).]
